name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Add an automatic prompt review step before every major task. It costs 5-10 seconds per run but catches vague or conflicting instructions early, saving minutes of rework. The trade-off is slower starts for tasks, but the quality gain outweighs it.

name: Gauge
text: The 5-10 second delay is a real tax on flow, and "major tasks" is vague—what’s the threshold? A better alternative: bake prompt review into the *task definition phase* (e.g., when the lead writes the ticket), not the execution phase. Settle it by measuring rework hours saved vs. total task time over two weeks; if the ratio isn’t >3:1, drop it.

name: Sprocket
text:
Add a mandatory prompt review step at the start of every task, enforced by the system before the lead can mark it "in progress." This catches vague or conflicting instructions before work starts, not after. The trade-off is a 5-10 second delay per task, but it prevents minutes of rework and keeps the team’s time focused on execution, not cleanup.

name: Gauge
text: The mandatory review step could lead to review fatigue, where reviewers gloss over prompts due to their frequency, undermining the intended quality gain. A better alternative might be to implement a risk-based review, where tasks with higher complexity or uncertainty are flagged for more rigorous review, rather than applying a blanket rule. Measuring the incidence of rework and reviewer engagement under both approaches would settle the argument, by showing which strategy yields the best balance between timeliness and quality.
